correctness.rationale: The valence-exceptional vertex set is intrinsically finite and invariant, so any homeomorphism permutes essential open edges; an iterate preserves each, and compactness forces an omega-limit point into its closure. Avoiding that closure disqualifies full-measure and residual basins. Conversely, for every closed target meeting all edge closures, explicit polynomial increasing interval homeomorphisms fix the target and send every nonfixed point to a target endpoint, except countably many repelling gap midpoints and ambient edge endpoints. Derivative lower bounds 1/2 and displacement bounds prove gluing continuity. The exceptional set is null and meagre; local open basins at every target point give minimality against any closed omitted-target set. The circle follows by cutting at a target point. The standalone rational checker confirms algebraic identities and finite cases but is not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A recent primary paper explicitly leaves a branched-continuum homeomorphic Milnor-attractor classification open after demonstrating only a tripod obstruction. Finite graphs form a natural broad family containing all tripods, branched trees and loops. The exact edge-incidence classification is a complete invariant with a simple graphical test, simultaneously handles both measure and category global attractors, and explains why branch points destroy universal closed-set realizability. This answers a motivating, structurally nontrivial special class rather than reparameterizing a known theorem. It deliberately does not claim general continua, prescribed nontrivial target dynamics, or nonhomeomorphic maps.
